title: Nykaa Profit Triples as Beauty Boom Lifts Q1; India VC Funding Dips in July
excerpt: FSN E-Commerce reported a more than three-fold jump in net profit to Rs 79.76 crore for Q1 FY27, while venture capital funding in India fell 61% month-on-month in July to $804 million.
body:
• Nykaa's net profit surged over 3X to Rs 79.76 crore in Q1 FY27, with revenue rising 29% to Rs 2,782 crore on strong beauty and fashion demand.
  • Consolidated GMV hit Rs 5,590 crore, up 34% year-on-year, while EBITDA grew 68% to Rs 236 crore—both 12-quarter highs.
  • India's VC ecosystem raised $804 million across 98 deals in July, down 61% from June's CRED-fueled $2.08 billion but up 29% from July 2025.
  • Analysts flag the absence of large AI startup rounds as a structural drag on India's venture funding momentum.

Nykaa Posts Strongest Quarter in Three Years

FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of Nykaa, reported a more than three-fold rise in consolidated net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, according to results released on Tuesday. Net profit climbed to Rs 79.76 crore from Rs 24.47 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the company's regulatory filing.

Revenue from operations rose 29% year-on-year to Rs 2,782 crore, up from Rs 2,154.94 crore a year earlier. Consolidated gross merchandise value touched Rs 5,590 crore for the quarter, reflecting 34% year-on-year growth. EBITDA jumped 68% to Rs 236 crore, according to Reuters.

"This quarter marked continued acceleration in our growth momentum and EBITDA margins, both reaching their highest levels in the last 12 quarters."

— Falguni Nayar, Founder, Executive Chairperson and CEO, Nykaa

Fashion Vertical Drives the Surge

The breakout performer was Nykaa's fashion segment, which posted net sales value growth in the mid-fifties and net revenue growth of nearly 50%—a multi-quarter high. Management attributed the turnaround to fewer returns and cancellations, an expanded brand portfolio across men's, women's, kids', and home categories, and an early payoff from its premium partnership with Nike.

The core beauty and personal care vertical, still Nykaa's largest revenue driver, delivered net sales value and revenue growth in the late twenties, according to the company's business update. In-house brands including Kay Beauty, Nykaa Cosmetics, and Dot & Key continued to gain market share, supporting longer-term gross margin expansion.

Analysts at Jefferies said continued strength across both beauty and fashion should support profitability, while CLSA noted that improving conversion from gross merchandise value to net sales value and strong customer acquisition had driven the sharp acceleration in fashion, Reuters reported.

Offline Expansion and Strategic Acquisition

Nykaa expanded its physical retail footprint to 324 stores as of June 30, up from 313 at the end of March, spanning 99 cities. The company also announced it will acquire a 51% stake in Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand, for a cash consideration of Rs 32 crore, according to YourStory.

The offline push is part of Nykaa's broader "phygital" strategy aimed at lowering long-term customer acquisition costs. Physical retail performance grew roughly 15% during the quarter, supported by healthier same-store sales, per company disclosures.

VC Funding Falls After CRED-Driven June Surge

Separately, venture capital funding in India's startup ecosystem declined sharply in July. Indian startups raised $804 million across 98 deals during the month, a 61% drop from the $2.08 billion recorded in June, which was inflated by CRED's $900 million mega round, according to YourStory Research.

However, funding was up 29.4% compared to July 2025, when total VC inflows stood at $621 million. Two deals propped up the July total: logistics platform Udaan secured $160 million and AI company Emergent raised $130 million.

Industry observers pointed to the absence of large AI startup fundraises as a structural headwind. While AI companies have attracted the bulk of venture capital globally—86% of US VC went to AI companies in the first half of 2026, according to LinkedIn's CREDX tracker—that trend has not yet materialized in India, where examples like Sarvam and Emergent remain exceptions rather than the norm.

Diaspora Lens: What the Numbers Mean

For NRIs tracking Indian markets, Nykaa's results underscore the resilience of India's premium consumer economy. The company's stock hit a 52-week high of Rs 319.80 on the NSE following the business update, a signal that institutional investors see further upside in India's organized beauty and fashion retail market.

The VC funding picture is more nuanced. While month-on-month declines look steep, the year-on-year improvement suggests Indian startups are on a steadier footing than in 2025. For diaspora investors and founders, the takeaway is clear: capital is available, but tilted toward proven business models and sectors with global tailwinds, particularly fintech and cleantech.

What's Next

Nykaa's final audited Q1 FY27 results will be the key watch for EBITDA margin trajectory, given the elevated marketing spend to fuel the fashion segment's breakout. On the VC front, industry watchers expect a late-year pickup in funding if macroeconomic conditions stabilize and more Indian AI startups reach scale. The first seven months of 2026 suggest total annual VC funding is unlikely to match the $13.2 billion recorded in 2024, per YourStory data.
nri_angle: Nykaa's strong Q1 signals resilience in India's premium consumer market for NRI investors, while the VC funding landscape favors proven models over early-stage bets.
